A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same PICA and VIAE research. Both contain readable main text, Table 1, Figures 1–8, and Appendices A–D, supporting a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic PICA results, VIAE generation and transfer experiments, MNIST classifier accuracies, and qualitative CelebA results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including Table 1's classifier results and the CelebA generation and transfer examples.

M1.justification: The PICA procedure, VIAE architecture and ELBO, and seen/unseen environment-transfer procedures are retained. Equation 2 factors the existing joint likelihood; the added CelebA architecture attribution does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Gaussian synthetic example, SMNIST square-location environments, SCMNIST color environments, and CelebA subpopulation transfer. CelebA's addition to the abstract summarizes experiments already present in v2 Appendix D.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same four linear classifiers using invariant or environmental features. Newly cited representation-learning methods are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The stated sample sizes, environment definitions, data partitions, classifier evaluation, and generation procedures remain unchanged. PICA still uses 1,000 samples per environment and one retained dimension. The new CelebA architecture description supplies previously undisclosed information.

E4.justification: The latent-space classifier analysis, seen/unseen transfer demonstrations, SCMNIST failure example, and CelebA case studies are retained. No ablation, robustness test, or empirical supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 as mean ± standard deviation over ten runs and explicitly describe training VIAE from scratch ten times. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values are identical, including invariant-feature label accuracies of 0.845 ± 0.050 and 0.832 ± 0.072. The empirical images in Figures 2, 4, 6–8 and their reported findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 corrects erroneous component indices in the Gaussian KL expressions. Appendix C.3.1 revises the MSE targets from X_et to X_e, explicitly states the latent-variable MSE objective, and corrects the final estimator's input to X_es. These are local derivation corrections; the main assumptions and PICA analysis remain intact.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion now include CelebA among the demonstrations supporting effectiveness, modestly broadening the headline empirical claim using evidence already in v2's appendix. The unsupervised IRM framework, PICA, VIAE, and intervention contributions are retained.

C2.justification: The closing interpretation of the classifier experiment changes from asserting effective downstream supervised IRM applicability in v2 Section 4.5 to motivating possible use of similar methods in v3 Section 4.4. The existing unseen-environment limitations and qualitative fairness qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly identifies Subramanian's PyTorch-VAE architecture as the basis for the decoder and invariant encoder, with reduced environmental encoders. This improves implementation disclosure without establishing a changed setting. The paper's existing code-access link remains.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds prior unsupervised invariant-representation work by Lopez, Moyer, Sun, and Muandet. Appendix D adds fair-representation references by Zemel, Creager, and Locatello; causal-representation and implementation references are also added. The Wasserstein reference is removed. These contextual additions retain the existing IRM positioning.

P1.justification: The title becomes 'Unsupervised Representation Learning – an Invariant Risk Minimization Perspective.' Architecture subsections are consolidated, seen/unseen transfer subsections are merged, and acknowledgments are added. Citation style and localized wording change, while most prose and the overall section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v3 adopts ICLR headers and heading styling, rearranges objective/constraint displays, enlarges Figure 1's labels, and rescales several figures. Figure 7 moves to a separate page. All eight figures and the existing table organization are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves research context, supplies a useful CelebA implementation attribution, and corrects local appendix expressions. Its more cautious downstream-IRM interpretation better matches Table 1's unchanged evaluation on training environments. These changes improve precision and transparency without substantially altering the paper's evidence or theoretical support.
